title: Man who stabbed family had mental-health problems
article: They were a patchwork family, and by most estimates a happy one. Even after the birth of their two youngest children, Leslie and Richard Kelly's family grew.
Several years ago, they took in Mr. Kelly's 11-year-old son from a previous relationship, and after his mother died in August, they took in his 13-year-old half-brother.

The family of six easily filled their small apartment on Glen Street in Oshawa, until early Saturday evening, when Gino Petralia allegedly barged through their door and used a hammer and a kitchen knife to reduce their numbers to five.
Neighbours identified Mr. Petralia as the father of Mr. Kelly's 13-year-old half-brother, Steven.
They said he had a history of mental-health problems, and had threatened the young family several times since they'd taken custody of Steven.
Mr. Petralia had been known to police for nearly 15 years, and had incurred three assault convictions stemming from incidents in 2004 and 1998, according to documents obtained by CTV Toronto.

The documents show that in January, he was convicted of breaching his probation and then charged with dangerous operation of a motor vehicle and causing a disturbance after he drove a motorized scooter erratically through a Whitby traffic court office while screaming.
He was scheduled to reappear in court on Dec. 23.

A family friend who asked not to be named said Mr. Petralia entered the home with a hammer, striking 5-year-old Riley Kelly before grabbing a knife from the kitchen and stabbing 3-year-old Nathan Kelly. She said he then turned the knife on the young couple as they rushed to protect their children.
Ms. Kelly, 26, died shortly after, and Nathan was in critical condition last night at Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children.
Mr. Kelly, 29, and Riley remained in serious condition.
Sue Cameron watched from her home across the street as Mr. Petralia dashed from the Kellys' home to an apartment a few doors down, where Steven's mother had lived until she died of a heart attack.
Through a glass door, she watched Mr. Petralia struggle in the home's hallway with a police officer and then dash out into the street only to be chased back into the hallway.
Moments later, she heard a bang.
Mr. Petralia, 47, was fatally shot by police. Special Investigations Unit officers confirmed that several shots were fired.

Peter Casha, a long-time neighbour of the Kellys, said he arrived at the scene moments after Mr. Petralia was shot. He had been a friend of Mr. Kelly's mother, and said that in the brief time she dated Mr. Petralia he "beat her up a couple of times.
"It's lucky the police killed him," he said.

Neighbours told him that Mr. Petralia shouted "If I can't have him, you can't have him either!" shortly before he was gunned down, and Mr. Casha said he was saddened but not entirely surprised by the attacks.
Neighbours said Mr. Petralia had worked for Lear Whitby until about 10 years ago, when his struggles with mental health worsened.
On Sunday evening, Mr. Kelly's status on his Facebook page was updated from a mobile phone to, "Trying to pull through so sorry babe i tried."
Neighbours said Mr. Kelly had worked numerous jobs to support his family, for a taxi company, a tow-truck company and FedEx.
On his Facebook profile, under activities, he wrote, "Currently help out with Rogers TV once in a while hopefully will make a career out of it so the wife will not need to work any more."
Autopsies of both bodies are scheduled for today.
